The invention of the light bulb is a complex historical topic. While Thomas Edison is often popularly credited with inventing the light bulb, he was not the only one involved in its development. Joseph Swan, a British inventor, independently developed a working incandescent lamp around the same time as Edison. In fact, many inventors contributed to the development of incandescent lamps before Edison, including Humphry Davy and Warren de la Rue. Edison is best known for creating a practical and commercially viable version of the light bulb, but he did not invent the concept itself.
